mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that triggers equity sell-offs due to reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a negative S&P 500 return over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an impending slowdown in manufacturing output, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate profits.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, INDPRO declines do not produce negative SPX returns in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC for INDPRO in this regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which consistently drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent inflationary pressures that prompt central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a tightening monetary policy cycle with disinflation, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced liquidity and growth concerns.
failure_condition: The joint condition of rising FEDFUNDS and falling CPIAUCSL fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market regime (UNRATE < 4.5%), a decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals an unexpected labor market slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors fear reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: In tight labor markets, PAYEMS declines do not produce negative SPX returns in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC for PAYEMS in this regime is below 0.03.
